item.title: 'Tell us where to come, schools fixed before our visit': CJP mocks Rajasthan govt
item.description: Mentioning the Ranka's post, another CJP member Sourav Das quipped: "People of Rajasthan, tell us where you want us to come. Government is releasing and fixing places before our visit!" Last month, Ranka alleged that Rajasthan Police was keeping a watch on people entering and leaving his house, hours after the organisation’s team faced a confrontation during its campaign to inspect government schools.

item.title: Why parents keep old report cards and childhood drawings, according to psychology
item.description: For parents, childhood drawings and school assignments go beyond mere artifacts of nostalgia; they encapsulate rich autobiographical memories and poignant family moments. Studies reveal that nostalgic feelings can elevate the perceived value of these everyday objects. Furthermore, these keepsakes serve as visual reminders of the swift journey through parenthood, capturing the essence of time spent in care and love.
item.dc:creator: TOI LIFESTYLE DESK

item.title: Atlanta man arrested after phone wipe; new ruling allows border searches
item.description: US border agents can now search traveler cellphones without reasonable suspicion or a warrant. A recent court ruling affirmed this broad authority at international borders. This decision follows an incident where a phone was wiped during an airport search. The ruling impacts traveler privacy and government access to electronic data. It highlights ongoing debates about digital device searches at the border.

item.title: Home guard slaps and drags woman by hair, arrested in Hyderabad
item.description: A home guard was terminated and arrested for assaulting a woman near Hafeezpet railway station, with the entire episode captured on video. Cyberabad police commissioner Ramesh acted swiftly, ordering the termination and the registration of a criminal case. Following the footage’s release, Director General of Police CV Anand emphasized a zero-tolerance policy towards crimes against women.

item.title: Red Pawns, Red Soldiers: How the Bolsheviks built a chess superpower
item.description: In his latest Grandmaster View column, India’s young GM Aarav Dengla looks back at how the Bolsheviks transformed chess from a pastime of Russia’s aristocracy into an instrument of mass education, military training and cultural revolution. From Ilyin-Zhenevsky and the Red Army to Botvinnik, Tal, Karpov and Kasparov, Aarav traces how a century-old state-backed experiment helped build the Soviet chess machine, and a legacy that still shapes the chess world today.
item.dc:creator: AARAV DENGLA

item.title: ‘Sell your wife’: Delhi's killer couple who murdered executive face fraud probe
item.description: Police probing the murder of Adani Realty project manager Yuvraj Singh Manchanda are examining whether he knew about an alleged fraud racket involving his former colleague Anya Vats and her partner Sanyam Sachdeva. An FIR details how the duo allegedly duped a senior executive of over Rs 1.2 crore using fake government notices, while investigators examine their movements and electronic devices.

item.title: Meet the 25-year-old who left air hostess job to become Himachal's first woman truck driver
item.description: It’s not easy to switch careers! But a young girl from Himachal Pradesh left her air hostess training to become a truck driver. Meet 25-year-old Neha Thakur who chose a career path few would have expected. After graduating, she worked briefly in the aviation sector and today, she spends her days behind the wheel of a 16-tonne truck, travelling across India. Neha belongs from Khudla village in Sarkaghat, Mandi district, Himachal Pradesh. She is widely known as Himachal Pradesh’s first woman truck driver. She covers her journeys in her own social-media videos and vlogs.

item.title: Numbers behind DUSU result: CJP momentum doesn’t show up in Left’s vote tally
item.description: The DUSU election results highlighted a contest that extended beyond the traditional ABVP NSUI binary, with Independent Deepanshu Shokeen’s decisive vice presidential victory and close races in the presidential and joint secretary contests. The results also showed a decline in the AISA SFI alliance’s vote tally despite its prominent participation in CJP mobilisations and campaigns around student issues such as housing, examinations and accountability.
item.dc:creator: SUGANDHA JHA

item.title: Turkey offers support to Saudi military as Houthi attacks test new defence pact
item.description: Amid rising Houthi threats, Turkey extends military aid to Saudi Arabia, potentially putting the new Saudi-Turkey-Pakistan defense agreement to the test. This pact ensures collective defense among member nations under attack. However, Pakistan has confirmed that there are no immediate plans for military action. Additionally, Saudi Arabia is pursuing military support from the US to counter the Houthis’ aggression.

item.title: Olympiad: Erigaisi picks first win of tournament; India's winning juggernaut rolls on
item.description: Arjun Erigaisi bounced back from a difficult start to the Chess Olympiad with a convincing victory over Maksim Chigaev, helping defending champions India beat Spain 3-1 in Round 4. Gukesh continued his impressive run, while Praggnanandhaa and Nihal Sarin drew. India’s women also remained unbeaten, beating Mongolia 3-1 as both Indian teams maintained their winning momentum in Samarkand.

item.title: 'Nothing is wrong': Salman Khan's BB 20 promo sparks health concerns
item.description: Bigg Boss host Salman Khan took to social media to clarify recent concerns about his health following a dramatic promo release. He revealed that the chest pain depicted was merely a message directed at contestant Qazi and expressed his displeasure with how the promo was edited, emphasizing its misleading nature. Addressing online trolls, Khan boldly removed his hat and shirt to confront critics of his appearance.
